items.title: 53571_Mary Lou Williams oral history interview
items.q: He used to live down the street from me and on his way to the subway he would pass here every day.

ctx.x: lyric to Father Woods and he said, no, they didn't capture the spirit of St. Martin. So I told him, "Well, you do it." He said, "I never wrote anything in poetry in my life, Mary, and can't do it." I said, "I'll tap it out for you." I did and he wrote a very beautiful lyric, he did, he wrote it. He had never written one before. So I asked him, "Let's do a blues." He said, "O.K." I said, "I'll get some slang words from Babs Gonzales." He said, "O.K." I said, "I'll call you tomorrow night." When I called back with…

But getting back to Babs Gonzales, you know I haven't told you something about this terrific character that's so fantastic. He wrote some of the greatest books on the slang idiom. He became so abused and confused about people taking his compositions and things that he had written He used to live down the street from me and on his way to the subway he would pass here every day. He said, "Listen Mary, I've written a book." He took this book to a disc jockey... This guy used his entire book and had it published…
